question: What energy density does the anode-free sodium full cell reach, and how does it compare with the theoretical maximum of LiCoO2/graphite cells?
trap: the ~200 Wh/kg of earlier SIB full cells
rendered:
Document: "Anode-Free Sodium Battery through in Situ Plating of Sodium Metal"

The anode-free sodium full cell reaches an energy density of ∼400 Wh/kg. This is stated on page 1 of the document, under the section "Building upon this anode-free architecture, we demonstrate a full cell using a pre-sodiated pyrite cathode to achieve energy densities of ∼400 Wh/kg, far surpassing recent reports on SIBs and even the theoretical maximum for LIB technology (387 Wh/kg for LiCoO2/graphite cells) while still relying on naturally abundant raw materials and cost-effective aqueous processing."

This means that the anode-free sodium full cell has an energy density that is greater than the theoretical maximum of LiCoO2/graphite cells.
